headline: UPDATE to totw-20261029-0700-06 (Aden airport attacks) -- Aden international airport reopens after temporary closure
dek: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM] Yemen's transport minister announced Aden international airport has resumed operations after its temporary closure. The airport was closed Oct 28 after Ansar Allah (Ansar Allah) launched ballistic missiles at it -- the 6th attack on Aden airport in the current campaign (0700-06).
sources: Yemen's transport minister, via Al Jazeera liveblog
fault_line: Reopening an airport under missile fire: resilience or a target inviting the next strike?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM] Yemen's transport minister announced Aden international airport has resumed operations after its temporary closure. The airport was closed Oct 28 after Ansar Allah (Ansar Allah) launched ballistic missiles at it -- the 6th attack on Aden airport in the current campaign (0700-06). Reopening is a resumption, not an end to the threat: the same AJ liveblog hour records Ansar Allah claiming 101 air strikes in the past 24 hours (10:15 GMT) and government air strikes on a Ansar Allah camp west of Taiz (12:20 GMT, see 1700-06). No casualty or damage update for the Aden strike itself is given in this entry.
sections.what_verified: Al Jazeera (T2, STATE QA) relaying the Yemeni transport minister -- 1 declared family, the announcing authority's own statement via one carrier.
sections.what_disputed: Reopening does not mean safe: Aden was attacked 6 times in this campaign and Saudi airports remain under repeated missile/drone attack (Riyadh Oct 10 terminal strike killed at least a dozen per Oct 23 reporting). No independent flight-operations confirmation retrieved in-window.
sections.why_matters: Aden airport is flying again hours after the 6th Ansar Allah missile attack on it -- the reopening that proves the Yemen air war is now routine.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE to totw-20261029-0700-06 (Aden airport attacks) -- Aden international airport reopens after temporary closure
